name: io.github.HuangGoodmanAgency/edgar-and-edgarette
title: SEC EDGAR Filings MCP: Edgar & Edgarette
description: SEC EDGAR filings for AI, no key: same-day 8-K events, company cards, merger fees, sealed forecasts.

limit.description: max rows, default 50, ceiling 200 — the reply carries total/returned/truncated, and `more` links the full board

tools.name: watch_company
tools.description: Follow a company's SEC filings: returns feed links to read whenever needed — the SEC's own Atom feed of every filing, plus Edgar & Edgarette's card and its JSON. Argument: company (name, ticker) or cik. No email is sent and nothing is stored.

company.description: company name as it files, or ticker

tools.name: price_program
tools.description: Price the program a filing usually calls for (e.g. mergers -> welcoming the new team; cmo-moves -> a new leader's launch), live from the POPS4 catalogue at wholesale. Returns total, per head, tier band, links to price it further, and the person who confirms it: Jenny Huang Goodman MPA MSc MHSA, Principal.

tools.name: get_company_performance
tools.description: Edgar & Edgarette performance card for any SEC filer (name, ticker or CIK): recent filings, then an actuarial-style reading of its audited 10-K figures (exposure, experience, credibility, an if-the-pace-held range, cautions). Every figure is the company's own, from SEC EDGAR, with source links. Reporting, not investment advice. From POPS4; confirmations: Jenny Huang Goodman MPA MSc MHSA, Principal.

price.description: optional share price YOU supply. Adds price/earnings, price/book, price/sales, dividend yield and market value, computed from that price and the company's filed per-share figures. The price is never stored or published; the card sources none.

tools.name: get_brand_record
tools.description: Answers: what is this company’s brand record, as filed? For any US SEC filer (name, ticker or CIK): every name it has filed under with dates (renames told apart from style-only changes), tickers and exchanges, and its brand-moving 8-K filings (officer changes, charter amendments, acquisitions, control changes, material agreements, cybersecurity incidents), each linked to the filing, with a one-line answer and a citation line for media. From SEC EDGAR via POPS4. Free, CC BY 4.0.

tools.name: why_sales_moved
tools.description: Answers: why did this company's sales move? From its newest 10-Q or 10-K: the filed sales change, the filed figures that explain it (segments, regions, units, price, volume), management's own words quoted exactly, whether the filed numbers back that explanation (verdict + evidence), POPS4's own reading labelled as such, and what to watch next. Every quote is checked word for word against the filing and every number against the filing. Covers the companies with a record; call with no company for the list. Reporting, not advice. Free, CC BY 4.0.

company.description: ticker, company name or CIK; leave empty for the list of companies with a record

tools.name: what_just_happened
tools.description: Answers: what did public companies just tell the SEC? Corporate events from the SEC's live filing feed, within about 15 minutes of the SEC accepting each filing: earnings releases (with the press release link), CEO/CFO and director changes, shareholder vote results, deals closed, material agreements, auditor changes and restatements, cybersecurity incidents, bankruptcies, delisting notices, restructurings, and 10-Q/10-K reports. Each event has the company, ticker, the SEC item code, the time the SEC accepted it, and the official SEC link. Filter by type, ticker or time. Free, CC BY 4.0. Reporting, not investment advice.

type.description: optional, comma-separated: earnings, leadership, vote-results, deal-completed, control-change, agreement, auditor, restatement, cyber, bankruptcy, delisting, restructuring, impairment, quarterly-report, annual-report (full list at https://www.pops4.com/boards/now/types.json)

since.description: optional ISO time; only events the SEC accepted after it

tools.name: get_ai_leaders
tools.description: AI Leaders: 12 US public companies in the AI business, read from their own SEC annual reports — revenue, growth, operating margin, research spending, equity, return on equity, Edgarette’s 80% revenue range. No prices, no ratings. Free, CC BY 4.0.

tools.name: get_energy_leaders
tools.description: Renewable & Geothermal Energy: 12 US public companies in solar, wind, grid, fuel cells and geothermal, read from their own SEC annual reports — the same fields as get_ai_leaders. No prices, no ratings. Free, CC BY 4.0.

tools.name: get_etf_health
tools.description: Look through a US-registered ETF (e.g. SPY, QQQ, DIA, IWM, XLF): its latest SEC N-PORT holdings, each stock matched to its SEC filer, and Health Watch (late filings, bankruptcy, listing notices, restructuring, impairments, cyber incidents, auditor changes) on the largest holdings, with the share of the fund they represent. For stock funds: a fund under half in common stock (bond, cash or fund-of-funds) returns coverage.covered = false and no boat. Display only, not a rating. Free, CC BY 4.0.

tools.name: get_etf_league
tools.description: Answers: which major US ETFs carry the fewest warning signs right now? SPY, QQQ, DIA, IWM and the 11 sector funds, each read through its latest SEC N-PORT holdings: boat (number of warning signs, each named), share of the fund in companies with warning filings, top-10 weight, effective holdings, largest sector and share checked. Ordered fewest signs first. No combined grade; display only, not a rating. Free, CC BY 4.0.

tools.name: get_continuation_funds
tools.description: Answers: who is raising private-equity continuation funds? Every Form D / D/A in the last 12 months that names a continuation fund or vehicle, one row per fund (latest filing), with the amounts the fund itself reported: total offering, amount sold so far, first-sale date, state, and a link to the filing. Shows who is raising, not the size of the secondary market. Free, CC BY 4.0.

tools.name: get_portfolio_health
tools.description: Read a whole stock portfolio through SEC filings: give a 13F filer’s CIK (a pension fund or manager) or a list of holdings [{ticker, weight}]. Funds are looked through to their N-PORT holdings. Returns Health Watch warning share, concentration (top 10, effective holdings), sector mix, Edgarette’s revenue-range width, cash conversion, growth, dividends, equity ratio, the Cash Compass mix, the Health Harbor boat, overlap and risks. Display only, not a rating. Free, CC BY 4.0.

cik.description: SEC CIK of a 13F filer, e.g. 714142

holdings.description: holdings with weights or dollar amounts

tools.name: get_cash_leaders
tools.description: This week’s cash leaders from audited SEC filings: the top 20 US companies ($2B+) by cash returned to owners (dividends + net buybacks ÷ market value), by operating cash earned ÷ market value, and by expected return among steady earners (income yield + Edgarette’s 80% revenue range). Also short-term places (Treasury-bill, floating-rate and ultra-short funds from their N-PORT filings: monthly returns, worst month, holdings mix) and monthly dividend payers (10-K verified, with yield, coverage, leverage, book value change, dividend cuts and warning signs). Every company passes a soundness screen first: no warning filing in 12 months, assets greater than liabilities, 4+ audited years. Ranked screens, not recommendations; prices are the latest quarter-end 13F prices.

tools.name: get_reinsurer_strength
tools.description: Reinsurer strength from SEC filings, for placing reinsurance: capital and growth, premiums and reserves to capital, five years of reserve development (Schedule VI: strengthened or released, % of opening reserves), accident-year loss ratio, return on capital, debt, investments to net reserves, warning filings, and a boat (count of six published warning signs). Property & casualty reinsurers plus RGA (life). A description from filings, not a rating; ratings and regulatory capital are not SEC data.

tools.name: get_sweep_record
tools.description: Kept its word: whether each place an actuary might sweep cash into did what it said, month by month, from SEC filings. Money-market funds (N-MFP3: SEC Rule 2a-7 liquidity and $1 price held every business day, 7-day yield), short-term Treasury and bond funds (N-PORT: months without a loss, worst month, compounded return), and monthly dividend payers (10-K: years the dividend held, yield, boat signs). Give a ticker for one record, or none for all. Facts from filings, not advice.

ticker.description: e.g. VMFXX, SGOV, O. Leave empty for every place.

tools.name: get_board_test
tools.description: The boards’ own calls, locked at the 6 Oct 2026 close with a SHA-256 receipt and scored against what happened: places for cash for 1, 3 and 6 months (paid what it said, no loss), cash cows and cash machines (beat the S&P 500 fund on total return, same dates), and Edgarette’s 12-month expected-return calls (landed inside her 80% range). A test of the boards, not advice.

tools.name: get_company_profile
tools.description: One document to build a company profile from, for any SEC filer (name, ticker or CIK): identity (CIK, ticker, LEI and FIGI where matched, SIC, exchange, fiscal year end), the method versions and restatement rule, the full Edgar & Edgarette card (filings, measures, Altman, Piotroski, Beneish, Sloan, the sealed 80% range, peers), and up to ten fiscal years of revenue, operating income, net income, cash flow, capital spending, R&D, dividends, assets, equity, cash, debt and EPS, each row carrying the 10-K it came from (accession number, form, filed date, XBRL tag, URL). Every figure is the company's own, from SEC EDGAR. Reporting, not investment advice. Schema pops4.profile/1; dictionary at /boards/profile/dictionary.json. From POPS4, Huang Goodman.

tools.name: seal_call
tools.description: Seal a call on a public company's next fiscal-year revenue beside Edgarette's own 80% range, before the annual report is filed. Give the company (ticker or CIK) and a low and high in whole US dollars. Returns a receipt: a hash of the company, the year, the range and the moment it was logged, on a public page. The call is graded inside or outside by the revenue in the company's next 10-K, the same filing that grades the house range. Free, no key, no name stored; refused once the annual report is on file. Call with only the company to read the house range and the calls already sealed. A statistical record, not a rating or a recommendation.

low.description: low end of the range, whole US dollars

high.description: high end of the range, whole US dollars

tools.name: get_debt_terms
tools.description: A company's debt, from its latest 10-K: principal due year by year (tagged maturity schedule), interest rates and covenants quoted from the debt note, the company's own interest-rate sensitivity from its market-risk section, interest paid, operating cash, later 10-Qs and debt 8-Ks, the 8-K agreements it signed, its auditor fees, and its merger adviser fees where it had a merger proxy. Same data as the treasury and credit reports on /boards/work/{ticker}. Argument: company (name, ticker or CIK).

tools.name: get_wall_street_fees
tools.description: The Price of Wall Street: every merger proxy (DEFM14A) with a fairness opinion in the last 12 months, read from SEC EDGAR. Each financial adviser's fee as the filing states it (estimate, maximum or contracted; opinion fee, closing-contingent part, credited fees never added twice), valuation methods and discount rates, with the passage. Arguments: adviser (optional, e.g. "Goldman Sachs") returns that adviser's engagements; company (optional) returns that deal; years (optional, 3 or 10) returns the year-by-year history; limit (default 25).

tools.name: get_bank_reconstruction
tools.description: A merger adviser's published valuation exhibits, re-computed by the house from the inputs the proxy discloses: the bank's range, the house's result, the difference, and the missing inputs. Not a fairness opinion and not a valuation view. Argument: case (optional, e.g. "001"); without it, the list of cases.

tools.name: get_deal_terms
tools.description: What merger contracts say the parties owe, from ten years of SEC merger proxies (DEFM14A): the target's termination fee, the buyer's reverse termination fee, committed debt financing, expense caps and each executive's golden-parachute total, each with the proxy's own sentence. Argument: company (name, ticker or CIK; optional). Without it, counts and the largest fees.

tools.name: get_country_record
tools.description: Answers: where is a company incorporated and headquartered, and which companies are tied to a country? From each company's own SEC record: state or country of incorporation, business and mailing address, and whether it files as a foreign private issuer (20-F, 40-F, 6-K). Arguments (all optional): company (name, ticker or CIK) for one company; country (e.g. Cayman Islands, Ireland, China) for every company incorporated or headquartered there; crosses_border true for companies incorporated in one country and run from another. Without arguments: counts by country. A place of incorporation is a legal fact, never a finding of wrongdoing.
